The decision will be made after consultation with the financial authorities 사진 확대 Korean Embassy in Washington, DC [Photo = Yonhap News] Discussions on rebuilding the embassy building in Washington, D.C., have been underway for the first time in more than 70 years.
 According to the National Assembly's Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee on the 16th, the Foreign Affairs and Trade Commission will discuss ways to include a new "reconstruction project of the Embassy of the United States" in the "Foreign Mission Facility Maintenance and Management Project" of the 2027 budget general account at the Budget Settlement Review Subcommittee on the 17th.
 The Korean Embassy building in the U.S., a symbol of diplomacy between South Korea and the U.S., was completed in 1954, and attention is being paid to whether major reconstruction will take place in more than 70 years as problems such as restrictions on diplomatic performance and increased maintenance and repair costs have been raised due to aging facilities.
 Based on the results of the basic plan and feasibility review service, the government plans to reflect a total of 300 billion won in project costs, including about 270 billion won in reconstruction projects and 30 billion won in temporary building rent to be used during the construction period.
 However, the reconstruction project of the embassy building in the U.S. is not immediately reflected in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' budget. This is because, unlike the renovation of government building facilities, new construction or full remodeling must be promoted through the National Property Management Fund under the Ministry of Finance and Economy.
 According to an official of the National Assembly's Foreign Affairs Committee, the committee will discuss the plan to adopt a side opinion that requires the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to discuss ways to rebuild the government building with the financial authorities instead of directly reflecting the reconstruction budget at the budget subcommittee on the 17th.
 As a result, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is expected to review whether to pursue the project and how to raise funds after consulting with the Ministry of Finance and Economy. As the related budget is under the jurisdiction of the National Assembly's Financial and Economic Planning Committee, additional consultations and deliberation procedures are needed until actual reconstruction.
